        venue: "arXiv 2024"
        core_method: "Learns per-layer adaptive threshold for MLP activation pruning based on input context, replacing fixed top-k selection"

        authors: "Mingyu Song, Liyao Jiang, Ye Tian, Shuai Yang, Zhongmin Cai"

        authors: "Mostafa Elhoushi, Akshat Shrivastava, Diana Liskovich, Basil Hosmer, Bram Wasti, Liangzhen Lai, Anas Mahmoud, Bilge Acun, Saurabh Agarwal, Ahmed Roman, Ahmed A Aly, Beidi Chen, Carole-Jean Wu"

    description: "Token importance and redundancy measurement approaches"

        authors: "Lianmin Chen, Jinhyuk Park, Lingfeng Shen, Yanbo Xu, Daniel Khashabi"
        year: 2024
        venue: "arXiv 2024"
        core_method: "Prunes visual tokens in VLMs based on attention scores after initial layers; discovers most visual tokens become redundant after layer 2"

        authors: "Sachin Goyal, Ziwei Ji, Ankit Singh Rawat, Aditya Krishna Menon, Sanjiv Kumar, Vaishnavh Nagarajan"
        year: 2024
        venue: "ICLR 2024"
        core_method: "Adds learnable <pause> tokens for extra computation without output; shows some positions genuinely need more compute"
        relation_to_carc: "Demonstrates compute demand varies per token. CARC is the inverse: removes compute from low-demand (redundant) tokens. Both validate non-uniform compute allocation."

        core_method: "Learns per-token routing to skip entire transformer blocks (both attention + MLP) via top-k capacity routing, implementing dynamic compute allocation"
        relation_to_carc: "Most related cross-axis work. Binary skip (all-or-nothing) vs CARC's graded sparsity (continuous). MoD requires training a router; CARC derives signal from KV similarity at inference time. MoD validates that some tokens need less cross-axis compute."
        verified: false

      - title: "LayerSkip: Enabling Early-Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding"
        authors: "Mostafa Elhoushi, Akshat Shrivastava, Diana Liskovich, Basil Hosmer, Bram Wasti, Liangzhen Lai, Anas Mahmoud, Bilge Acun, Saurabh Agarwal, Ahmed Roman, Ahmed A Aly, Beidi Chen, Carole-Jean Wu"
        year: 2024
        venue: "ACL 2024"
        core_method: "Early exit training + self-speculative decoding: draft tokens from early layers, verify with full model"
        relation_to_carc: "Layer-level exit is coarser than CARC's per-component sparsity. Both share insight that not all tokens need full computation. LayerSkip's exit decision could incorporate CARC's redundancy signal."
        verified: false

      - title: "ShortGPT: Layers in Large Language Models are More Redundant Than You Expect"
        authors: "Xin Men, Mingyu Xu, Qingyu Zhang, Bingning Wang, Hongyu Lin, Yaojie Lu, Xianpei Han, Weipeng Chen"
        year: 2024
        venue: "arXiv 2024"
        core_method: "Block Influence (BI) score measuring layer-wise hidden state similarity; prunes high-BI (high redundancy) layers with minimal quality loss"
        relation_to_carc: "Layer-level redundancy (static) vs CARC's token-level redundancy (dynamic). BI score is conceptually related to KV similarity but at different granularity. Complementary: ShortGPT prunes layers, CARC sparsifies within layers."
        verified: false

      - title: "Not All Tokens Are What You Need"
        authors: "Zhenyu Zhang, Mingjie Zhan, Yifan Hao, Damien Teney"
        year: 2024
        venue: "ICML 2024"
        core_method: "Filters training tokens by loss: removes high-loss (noisy) and low-loss (redundant) tokens, improving training efficiency and quality"
        relation_to_carc: "Validates that token redundancy matters for compute allocation (in training). CARC operationalizes the same intuition at inference using KV similarity. Conceptual support for redundancy-driven paradigm."
        verified: false

  redundancy-signal:
    description: "Token importance and redundancy measurement approaches"
    papers:
      - title: "Token Merging: Your ViT But Faster"
        authors: "Daniel Bolya, Cheng-Yang Fu, Xiaoliang Dai, Peizhao Zhang, Christoph Feichtenhofer, Judy Hoffman"
        year: 2023
        venue: "ICLR 2023"
        core_method: "Merges similar tokens based on key cosine similarity in attention, progressively reducing token count through ViT layers"
        relation_to_carc: "Uses key similarity as token redundancy signal — directly related to CARC's KV similarity. ToMe merges tokens (changes sequence structure); CARC modulates compute per token (preserves structure). ToMe for ViTs; CARC for autoregressive LLMs."
        verified: false

      - title: "FastV: An Image is Worth 1/2 Tokens After Layer 2"
        authors: "Lianmin Chen, Jinhyuk Park, Lingfeng Shen, Yanbo Xu, Daniel Khashabi"
        year: 2024
        venue: "arXiv 2024"
        core_method: "Prunes visual tokens in VLMs based on attention scores after initial layers; discovers most visual tokens become redundant after layer 2"
        relation_to_carc: "Shows token redundancy emerges early in forward pass and is detectable from attention patterns. CARC uses KV similarity for redundancy detection in text tokens. Supports the thesis that redundancy-driven pruning is effective."
        verified: false

      - title: "Think Before You Speak: Training Language Models With Pause Tokens"
        authors: "Sachin Goyal, Ziwei Ji, Ankit Singh Rawat, Aditya Krishna Menon, Sanjiv Kumar, Vaishnavh Nagarajan"
        year: 2024
        venue: "ICLR 2024"
        core_method: "Adds learnable <pause> tokens for extra computation without output; shows some positions genuinely need more compute"
        relation_to_carc: "Demonstrates compute demand varies per token. CARC is the inverse: removes compute from low-demand (redundant) tokens. Both validate non-uniform compute allocation."
        verified: false

      - title: "Scissorhands: Exploiting the Persistence of Importance Hypothesis for LLM KV Cache Compression at Test Time"
        authors: "Zichang Liu, Aditya Desai, Fangshuo Liao, Weitao Wang, Victor Xie, Zhaozhuo Xu, Anastasios Kyrillidis, Anshumali Shrivastava"
        year: 2024
        venue: "NeurIPS 2024"
        core_method: "Shows token importance (attention score) persists across decoding steps; evicts tokens not important in recent history"
        relation_to_carc: "Validates persistence of importance — related to CARC's EMA smoothing of redundancy. Scissorhands uses attention scores (O(n)); CARC uses KV similarity (O(1)). CARC's EMA encodes persistence by construction."
        verified: false

  evaluation:
    description: "Benchmarks and metrics for evaluating sparsity and efficiency methods"
    papers:
      - title: "Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset"
        authors: "Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Saurav Kadavath, Akul Arora, Steven Basart, Eric Tang, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt"
        year: 2021
        venue: "NeurIPS 2021"
        core_method: "12,500 competition math problems across 7 subjects, 5 difficulty levels"
        relation_to_carc: "Primary evaluation dataset. Extended reasoning chains ideal for studying token-level redundancy. MATH-500 subset used for MVP."
        verified: false

      - title: "Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems (GSM8K)"
        authors: "Karl Cobbe, Vineet Kosaraju, Mohammad Bavarian, Mark Chen, Heather Jun, Lukasz Kaiser, Matthias Plappert, Jerry Tworek, Jacob Hilton, Reiichiro Nakano, Christopher Hesse, John Schulman"
        year: 2021
        venue: "arXiv 2021"
        core_method: "8,500 grade school math problems requiring 2-8 step reasoning"
        relation_to_carc: "Secondary benchmark. Shorter reasoning chains; validates CARC across difficulty levels."
        verified: false

      - title: "Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU)"
        authors: "Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Steven Basart, Andy Zou, Mantas Mazeika, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt"
        year: 2021
        venue: "ICLR 2021"
        core_method: "57-subject multiple choice benchmark covering STEM, humanities, social sciences"
        relation_to_carc: "Knowledge-intensive short-context benchmark. Validates that CARC-driven sparsity doesn't degrade factual recall."
        verified: false

      - title: "LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding"
        authors: "Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li"
        year: 2024
        venue: "ACL 2024"
        core_method: "21 tasks across 6 categories for long context (4K-10K+ tokens)"
        relation_to_carc: "Critical for KV eviction evaluation. Long inputs stress-test whether CARC correctly identifies evictable tokens. Primary benchmark for O(1) KV eviction contribution."
        verified: false
